statement: Whenever check_valid_cuts(n, rectangles) returns a result r, r = true if and only if V(n, rectangles) or H(n, rectangles), where: V(n, rectangles) means there exist integers a,b with 0 <= a < b <= n such that (i) for every i with 0 <= i < m, not (sx_i < a < ex_i) and not (sx_i < b < ex_i); (ii) there exists i with ex_i <= a; (iii) there exists i with sx_i >= a and ex_i <= b; (iv) there exists i with sx_i >= b. H(n, rectangles) means there exist integers c,d with 0 <= c < d <= n such that (i) for every i, not (sy_i < c < ey_i) and not (sy_i < d < ey_i); (ii) there exists i with ey_i <= c; (iii) there exists i with sy_i >= c and ey_i <= d; (iv) there exists i with sy_i >= d.
preconditions: n and rectangles satisfy the problem constraints: n >= 3; m = len(rectangles) >= 3; each rectangles[i] has length 4; writing sx_i = rectangles[i][0], sy_i = rectangles[i][1], ex_i = rectangles[i][2], ey_i = rectangles[i][3] for 0 <= i < m, we have 0 <= sx_i < ex_i <= n and 0 <= sy_i < ey_i <= n; and for i != j the interiors are disjoint: not (sx_i < ex_j and sx_j < ex_i and sy_i < ey_j and sy_j < ey_i).

statement: For every n and rectangles satisfying the preconditions, the call check_valid_cuts(n, rectangles) returns a result r; it does not panic, get stuck, or overflow.
preconditions: n and rectangles satisfy the problem constraints: n >= 3; m = len(rectangles) >= 3; each rectangles[i] has length 4; writing sx_i = rectangles[i][0], sy_i = rectangles[i][1], ex_i = rectangles[i][2], ey_i = rectangles[i][3] for 0 <= i < m, we have 0 <= sx_i < ex_i <= n and 0 <= sy_i < ey_i <= n; and for i != j the interiors are disjoint: not (sx_i < ex_j and sx_j < ex_i and sy_i < ey_j and sy_j < ey_i).

statement: Let V(n, rectangles) mean that there exist integers a,b with 0 <= a < b <= n such that: (i) for every i with 0 <= i < m, not (sx_i < a < ex_i) and not (sx_i < b < ex_i); (ii) there exists i with ex_i <= a; (iii) there exists i with sx_i >= a and ex_i <= b; (iv) there exists i with sx_i >= b. If V(n, rectangles) holds, then check_valid_cuts(n, rectangles) returns true.

statement: If check_valid_cuts(n, rectangles) returns true, then check_valid_cuts(n, R') returns true.
preconditions: The original n and rectangles satisfy the problem constraints: n >= 3; m = len(rectangles) >= 3; each rectangles[i] has length 4; writing sx_i = rectangles[i][0], sy_i = rectangles[i][1], ex_i = rectangles[i][2], ey_i = rectangles[i][3] for 0 <= i < m, we have 0 <= sx_i < ex_i <= n and 0 <= sy_i < ey_i <= n; and for i != j the interiors are disjoint: not (sx_i < ex_j and sx_j < ex_i and sy_i < ey_j and sy_j < ey_i). Suppose that for every i, sx_i <= sx'_i < ex'_i <= ex_i and sy_i <= sy'_i < ey'_i <= ey_i.

statement: If check_valid_cuts(n, rectangles) returns true, then there exist two vertical cuts or two horizontal cuts such that every rectangle lies entirely in one of the three sections and each of the three sections contains exactly one rectangle. In symbols, either there exist integers a,b with 0 <= a < b <= n satisfying (i) for every i, not (sx_i < a < ex_i) and not (sx_i < b < ex_i), and such that the three sets L = {i | ex_i <= a}, M = {i | sx_i >= a and ex_i <= b}, R = {i | sx_i >= b} each have cardinality 1, or the analogous statement holds for y-coordinates with c,d and sets {i | ey_i <= c}, {i | sy_i >= c and ey_i <= d}, {i | sy_i >= d}.
preconditions: n and rectangles satisfy the problem constraints: n >= 3; m = len(rectangles) >= 3; each rectangles[i] has length 4; writing sx_i = rectangles[i][0], sy_i = rectangles[i][1], ex_i = rectangles[i][2], ey_i = rectangles[i][3] for 0 <= i < m, we have 0 <= sx_i < ex_i <= n and 0 <= sy_i < ey_i <= n; and for i != j the interiors are disjoint: not (sx_i < ex_j and sx_j < ex_i and sy_i < ey_j and sy_j < ey_i). Also m = 3.
